headline: House impeachment vote expected as soon as next week, multiple GOP sources expect it to pass
dek: CNN reports House Republicans are turning on Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth after the midterm rout, arguing he oversold a quick, easy win in Iran and helped convince Trump to attack with no exit strategy. Rep.
sources: CNN, citing Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Kentucky) on record and multiple anonymous Republican sources
fault_line: Scapegoat or accountability — did Hegseth mislead Trump with a quick-win promise, or is the party pinning its midterm defeat on the Pentagon chief to protect Trump?

sections.what_happened: CNN reports House Republicans are turning on Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth after the midterm rout, arguing he oversold a quick, easy win in Iran and helped convince Trump to attack with no exit strategy. Rep. Thomas Massie told CNN he plans to trigger a vote to impeach Hegseth when Congress returns next week, and multiple GOP sources told CNN they expect it to pass. House Republicans are also expected to vote to directly repudiate Hegseth in a matter of days. Hegseth, via a person close to him, still expects to stay and is prepared to fight an impeachment effort. NEW vs 0200-02 (which recorded Massie's pledge, Tillis's 'reckoning' quote and the White House full-confidence reply via USA Today): the passage expectation from GOP sources and the separate days-away repudiation vote are the new elements; the Massie trigger plan itself is not new.
sections.what_verified: CNN has NO declared tier in the source registry and therefore does NOT count toward corroboration. The Massie September articles and return-next-week plan were already recorded (0200-02) via USA Today, which is likewise untiered, so no declared family is added here.
sections.what_disputed: On the record against any reading that exit is decided: Trump told reporters Nov 4 Hegseth is 'doing a very good job' and told Fox he was not considering a Cabinet shakeup; White House spokesperson Anna Kelly stated Trump 'has full confidence in Secretary Hegseth'; Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said Hegseth is '100% committed' to leading until the end of Trump's term. Procedurally, House impeachment needs only a simple majority but Senate conviction needs two-thirds, so even a House vote passing would very likely not remove him; and the House remains Republican-controlled until the new Congress convenes Jan 3, 2027, so a passage expectation implies Republican defections, which CNN's anonymous sources do not quantify.
sections.why_matters: Update Short inside the proven Trump-Iran endgame lane, distinct from 0200-02: lead with GOP sources expecting the impeachment vote to pass plus the days-away repudiation vote, then land Trump's on-record denial and the Senate two-thirds bar in the same video. Never present removal as decided or likely.
